questions.scenario: Your family is finally doing the 'Griha Pravesh' (housewarming) for a new flat. What is your very first reaction when you walk in?

options.A: You pull out the compass app on your phone and walk to the main door to physically verify if it is exactly North-East facing.
options.B: You ask your dad for the builder's blueprint so you can mathematically calculate where the exact center of the house is.
options.C: You immediately start visualizing where to place the traditional Tulsi plant and which wall would look best painted a warm yellow.
options.D: You confidently tell your parents that buying this specific 'lucky' flat is going to bring huge financial growth to the family.

questions.scenario: Board exams are coming up, and your parents want you to rearrange your study table for 'better focus'. How do you do it?

options.A: You actively push the heavy wooden desk against the East wall so you can physically face the sunrise while studying.
options.B: You check the room's geometry to make sure your back isn't directly facing an open window or a sharp corner.
options.C: You decorate the table with a cute lucky bamboo plant, green sticky notes, and a neat lamp to create a super positive vibe.
options.D: You convince your sibling to swap rooms with you, arguing that this specific room's layout is highly beneficial for your exam results.

questions.scenario: Mummy scolds you at night because you are sleeping with your feet pointing towards the home Mandir (prayer room). You...

options.A: Quickly jump out of bed and physically rotate your mattress and pillows right then and there to fix the direction.
options.B: Research the Earth's magnetic fields on your phone to logically understand *why* the South-to-North sleeping rule exists.
options.C: Use this as an excuse to buy a new dreamcatcher, colorful bedsheets, and completely change the aesthetic of your sleeping area.
options.D: Tell Mom that we should just hire a carpenter next week to permanently fix the bed's position so it's always correct and problem-free.

questions.scenario: It's time for the massive Diwali Safai (deep cleaning). What is your main mission?

options.A: Walking through every room and actively throwing out old junk from the dark corners to clear out the 'blocked energy'.
options.B: Systematically making sure items are kept in their right elemental zones (e.g., ensuring the iron tools are kept far from the kitchen fire).
options.C: Hanging beautiful fresh flower torans, lighting diyas in specific corners, and making a colorful rangoli at the entrance.
options.D: Assigning specific cleaning tasks to your siblings and declaring the house '100% Diwali Ready' once the project is managed.

questions.scenario: Your family is setting up a small Mandir in a rented apartment. What is your contribution?

options.A: Using your phone to pinpoint the exact North-East corner of the hall and physically mounting the wooden shelf there.
options.B: Checking the architectural layout to guarantee the Mandir doesn't accidentally share a common wall with the bathroom.
options.C: Decorating the shelf with fresh marigold (genda) flowers, a shiny brass bell, and a beautifully painted colorful backdrop.
options.D: Managing the discussion on whether it's more cost-effective to buy a ready-made marble Mandir or get a custom wooden one built.

questions.scenario: Your Dadi (grandmother) gifts you a Laughing Buddha or a Feng Shui tortoise. What do you do with it?

options.A: Walk around the drawing room trying to find a solid, undisturbed physical spot where it won't be moved by the maid.
options.B: Read the exact placement rules to ensure the tortoise's face is positioned at a precise 45-degree angle to the main door.
options.C: Choose the most aesthetically pleasing crystal version that perfectly matches your living room's glass center table.
options.D: Tell your parents it's a great symbol of prosperity and suggest buying a matching pair for Dad's office desk to boost his business.

questions.scenario: You keep having bad dreams, and your family blames it on the 'heavy energy' in your bedroom. How do you solve it?

options.A: You physically push the heavy almirah (wardrobe) away from the bed because it feels like it's looming over you.
options.B: You sketch your room's layout on rough paper to see if your bed is accidentally crossing the room's invisible central axis.
options.C: You start burning fragrant incense sticks (agarbatti) and place a Himalayan salt lamp on your nightstand for a calming, peaceful vibe.
options.D: You convince your parents that the whole room needs a structural upgrade and ask for a budget to redesign it properly.

questions.scenario: A relative brings a wind chime from their vacation as a gift for your house. What happens next?

options.A: You grab a stool and a hammer, and instantly fix it on the main balcony frame where the wind hits the hardest.
options.B: You count the number of metal rods to analyze if it creates the precise sound frequency recommended for the West zone.
options.C: You add some fairy lights around the balcony door to make the wind chime look magical when it rings at night.
options.D: You realize wind chimes are super popular and think about how profitable it would be to start an online store selling lucky charms.

questions.scenario: Your family visits an empty plot of land that they want to buy to build a future home. What are you observing?

options.A: Walking across the dusty plot, checking the slope of the land with your feet and seeing where the sun sets.
options.B: Looking at the local map to analyze the shape of the plot (checking if it is a perfect rectangle or cut awkwardly from a corner).
options.C: Imagining where the beautiful green garden will be planted and how the morning sunlight will beautifully light up the living room.
options.D: Listening to the property dealer and using the plot's 'lucky East-facing' status to negotiate a smarter price.

questions.scenario: Your best friend feels their room has 'negative vibes' because they always feel lazy studying there. You tell them:

options.A: 'Let's open these specific windows right now. You need cross-ventilation to physically flush out the stagnant air!'
options.B: 'Your heavy bookshelf is in the wrong elemental zone, creating a feeling of weight on your head. Let's map it out.'
options.C: 'Let's paint these dark walls a bright, cheerful pastel color and keep a cute money plant on the window sill.'
options.D: 'If you fix this room's layout, your productivity will double, and you'll save hours of study time before the exams.'

Role_1.title: On-site Vastu Consultant
Role_1.primary_match_text: You are a hands-on action taker! You believe in physically shifting things, using your compass, and being present in the space to feel and fix the energy around you.
Role_1.day_in_the_life: Traveling to new plots, homes, and offices, measuring directions on the ground, and physically pointing out where the kitchen, bedroom, and heavy furniture should be shifted.
Role_1.alternative_match_text: Your active, hands-on nature also makes you great for Site Supervision, Civil Engineering, or Event Management.
Role_1.educational_roadmap: Take up any stream in 11th/12th (PCM or Arts preferred). Pursue a B.Arch (Architecture) or B.Sc in Interior Design. Add specific diploma courses in Vastu Shastra from recognized Indian institutes to become a certified consultant.

Role_2.title: Energy & Floor-Plan Analyst
Role_2.primary_match_text: You are the master of logic and geometry! You look at the invisible lines, calculate exact degrees, and balance the five elements (Panchamahabhuta) using pure math and rules.
Role_2.day_in_the_life: Sitting with massive builder blueprints, drawing grids on AutoCAD, calculating the exact Brahmasthan (center), and ensuring the layout mathematically aligns with natural forces.
Role_2.alternative_match_text: Your analytical and spatial skills make you highly suited for Urban Planning, Draftsmanship, or Mathematical Modeling.
Role_2.educational_roadmap: Opt for 11th/12th Science (PCM). Pursue a B.Arch (Architecture) or B.Tech in Civil Engineering. Follow this up with advanced certifications in MahaVastu or ancient Indian architectural sciences.

Role_3.title: Vastu Interior Designer
Role_3.primary_match_text: You are the creative soul of the house! You know that good energy isn't just about directions; it's about beautiful colors, soothing lighting, and the aesthetic placement of lucky objects.
Role_3.day_in_the_life: Selecting the perfect pastel paints for a bedroom, choosing indoor plants like money plants, and placing beautiful crystals and wind chimes to make a home feel like a peaceful temple.
Role_3.alternative_match_text: Your eye for beauty and energy makes you perfect for Interior Decorating, Set Design, or Art Therapy.
Role_3.educational_roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th works perfectly. Go for a Bachelor's in Interior Design (B.Des), B.Sc in Interior Design, or Fine Arts (BFA). Integrate short-term Feng Shui and Vastu aesthetic courses into your portfolio.

Role_4.title: Vastu Firm Founder / Real Estate Advisor
Role_4.primary_match_text: You are the boss with the big vision! You understand that 'Vastu-compliant' is a huge selling point in India, and you know how to advise clients, builders, and manage a profitable business around it.
Role_4.day_in_the_life: Meeting with top real estate builders, certifying new apartment complexes as '100% Vastu Compliant', consulting wealthy clients on plot purchases, and managing your own team of experts.
Role_4.alternative_match_text: Your negotiation and leadership skills translate perfectly to Real Estate Brokering, Business Consulting, or Entrepreneurship.
Role_4.educational_roadmap: Take Commerce or any stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a degree in BBA or B.Com, followed by an MBA in Real Estate Management or Marketing. Taking foundational Vastu diplomas will help you lead your firm with complete authority.
